questions.text: Which is the highest peacetime gallantry award in India?
questions.solution: Shortcut: 'Peace' = Ashoka (Emperor of Peace/Dharma Chakra) — Param Vir Chakra is *wartime* highest. Ashoka Chakra is peacetime equivalent. Step-by-step: Gallantry awards are categorized into Wartime (Param Vir Chakra, Maha Vir Chakra, Vir Chakra) and Peacetime (Ashoka Chakra, Kirti Chakra, Shaurya Chakra). Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime decoration for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield. Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime award.

questions.text: Introducing a boy, a girl said, 'He is the son of the only daughter of the father of my brother.' How is the boy related to the girl?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Decode backwards from the last relation. 'Father of my brother' = My Father. 'Only daughter of my Father' = Me (the speaker/girl). 'Son of me' = My Son. Worked Solution: The phrase 'father of my brother' refers to the girl's father. The 'only daughter' of that father is the girl herself (as she has no sisters implied by 'only daughter'). The boy is the 'son' of that daughter, making him the girl's son.

questions.text: How many Fundamental Duties are currently specified in the Constitution of India under Article 51A?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Option Elimination): Remember the amendment timeline. The 42nd Amendment (1976) added 10 duties. The 86th Amendment (2002) added 1 more duty regarding elementary education. Eliminate 10 (old count), 9, and 12. The correct total is 11. Full Solution: Fundamental Duties were incorporated in Part IV-A (Article 51A) by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, initially numbering 10. Subsequently, the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added the 11th duty: "Who is a parent or guardian to provide opportunities for education to his child or, as the case may be, ward between the age of six and fourteen years." Thus, the current total is 11.

questions.text: Who was the first Governor-General of India (after the Charter Act of 1833)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Distinguish 'Bengal' vs 'India' — Warren Hastings was first GG of *Bengal* (1773); Charter Act 1833 redesignated the post to GG of *India* — first holder was William Bentinck. Step-by-step: The Regulating Act 1773 created Governor-General of Bengal (Warren Hastings). The Charter Act 1833 changed the title to Governor-General of India. Lord William Bentinck (1833–1835) became the first to hold this new title. Lord Cornwallis and Lord Dalhousie served later.

questions.text: Under which Article of the Constitution of India is the 'Annual Financial Statement' (Union Budget) laid before Parliament?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): Article 110 defines 'Money Bill'. Article 112 mandates the 'Annual Financial Statement'. Article 114 deals with 'Appropriation Bills'. Article 116 covers 'Votes on Account, Votes of Credit and Exceptional Grants'. The keyword 'Statement' maps directly to Article 112. Step-by-step: Article 112 of the Constitution of India stipulates that the President shall in respect of every financial year cause to be laid before both Houses of Parliament a statement of the estimated expenditure and receipts of the Government of India. This statement is constitutionally termed the 'Annual Financial Statement' and is popularly known as the Union Budget.

questions.text: The value of tan 10° × tan 20° × tan 30° × tan 40° × tan 50° × tan 60° × tan 70° × tan 80° is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use complementary angle identity tan(90°−θ) = cot θ. Pair terms: (tan 10° × tan 80°) = tan 10° × cot 10° = 1. Similarly (20°,70°), (30°,60°), (40°,50°) each multiply to 1. Product = 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1. Step-by-step: tan 80° = cot 10°, tan 70° = cot 20°, tan 60° = cot 30°, tan 50° = cot 40°. Expression becomes (tan 10° cot 10°) × (tan 20° cot 20°) × (tan 30° cot 30°) × (tan 40° cot 40°) = 1 × 1 × 1 × 1 = 1.

questions.text: A body starts from rest and moves with a uniform acceleration of 4 m/s². The distance travelled by the body in the 5th second of its motion is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a body starting from rest (u=0), distance travelled in the nth second = a × (n - 0.5). Here, a = 4 m/s² and n = 5. Distance = 4 × (5 - 0.5) = 4 × 4.5 = 18 m. Full Solution: Using the formula for displacement in the nth second: S_n = u + (a/2)(2n - 1). Given u = 0, a = 4 m/s², n = 5. S_5 = 0 + (4/2)(2×5 - 1) = 2 × 9 = 18 m.

questions.text: The HCF and LCM of two numbers are 12 and 720 respectively. If one of the numbers is 60, what is the other number?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the fundamental relation Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM. The second number = (HCF × LCM) / First Number = (12 × 720) / 60. Cancel 60 with 720 to get 12, then 12 × 12 = 144. Step-by-step: Let the other number be x. We know HCF = 12, LCM = 720, and one number = 60. Formula: 60 × x = 12 × 720. Solving for x: x = (12 × 720) / 60 = 12 × 12 = 144.

questions.text: An iron nail is dipped in a solution of copper sulphate (CuSO₄) for some time. Which of the following observations is correct based on the reactivity series?

options.label: A
options.text: The blue colour of the solution intensifies

options.label: B
options.text: No change occurs in the solution

options.label: C
options.text: The blue colour fades and a reddish-brown deposit forms on the nail

options.label: D
options.text: The solution turns green and the nail dissolves completely

questions.solution: Shortcut: Recall reactivity series mnemonic '... Fe ... (H) ... Cu ...'. Iron (Fe) is above Copper (Cu), so Fe displaces Cu²⁺. Reaction: Fe + CuSO₄ → FeSO₄ + Cu. Blue Cu²⁺ fades (replaced by pale green Fe²⁺), reddish-brown Cu metal deposits on nail. Eliminate options showing no change or intensifying blue. Full Solution: Iron is more reactive than copper. It displaces copper from its salt solution forming ferrous sulphate (light green) and copper metal (reddish-brown). The blue colour of CuSO₄ fades as Cu²⁺ ions are reduced to Cu(s), which coats the nail.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of (7^95 − 3^58)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of 4 for unit digits. For 7^95: 95 ÷ 4 remainder 3 → unit digit of 7³ = 3. For 3^58: 58 ÷ 4 remainder 2 → unit digit of 3² = 9. Subtract: 3 − 9 = −6 → borrow 10 → unit digit 4. Step-by-step: Cyclicity of 7 is 7,9,3,1. 95 mod 4 = 3 → 3rd position = 3. Cyclicity of 3 is 3,9,7,1. 58 mod 4 = 2 → 2nd position = 9. Unit digit of difference = (10 + 3) − 9 = 4.

questions.text: Pointing to a man in a photograph, a woman said, 'He is the son of the only son of my grandfather.' How is the man related to the woman?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Draw family tree. 'Only son of my grandfather' = Woman's Father. 'Son of (Father)' = Woman's Brother (or herself, but 'He' implies male sibling). Worked Solution: Woman's Grandfather's only son is Woman's Father. The man is the son of Woman's Father. Therefore, the man is Woman's Brother.

questions.text: Directions: In each of the following questions, a statement is given followed by two conclusions. You have to take the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read the conclusion and decide which of the given conclusions logically follows from the given statements, disregarding common knowledge. Statements: Some stars are moons. All moons are planets. Conclusions: I. Some stars are planets. II. No planet is a star.
questions.solution: From 'Some stars are moons' and 'All moons are planets', we can infer that the intersection of stars and moons exists, and since all those moons are planets, some stars must be planets. Thus, Conclusion I follows. Conclusion II claims 'No planet is a star', which contradicts the inference from Conclusion I (since some stars are planets, it is false that no planet is a star).

questions.text: What is the largest planet in our solar system in terms of mass?
questions.solution: Jupiter is the largest planet in our solar system in terms of mass, with a mass approximately 318 times that of Earth.

questions.text: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid right circular cylinder of radius 4 cm. The height of the cylinder is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Volume remains constant during melting. Equate Volume of Sphere = Volume of Cylinder. (4/3)πr³ = πR²h. Cancel π. h = (4/3 × 6³) / 4² = (4/3 × 216) / 16 = 288 / 16 = 18 cm. Step-by-step: Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(6)³ = (4/3)π(216) = 288π cm³. Volume of cylinder = π(4)²h = 16πh cm³. Equating: 16πh = 288π => h = 288/16 = 18 cm.

questions.text: Exercise 'Dharma Guardian' is a joint military exercise conducted between the Indian Army and the army of which country?
questions.solution: Shortcut (Elimination Technique): 'Shakti' is with France (B). 'AustraHind' is with Australia (C). 'Ajeya Warrior' is with UK (D). 'Dharma Guardian' is the specific annual exercise with Japan (A) focusing on counter-terrorism and disaster relief. Step-by-step: Exercise Dharma Guardian is a bilateral joint military exercise between the Indian Army and the Japan Ground Self-Defense Force (JGSDF). It commenced in 2018 and is held annually in alternating locations (India and Japan). It focuses on sharing best practices in counter-terrorism operations, jungle warfare, and Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR) under UN mandate.
